featured_reviews.name: Jainam
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this to warn everyone about the severe lack of safety and basic humanity at Roxy Cinema. Yesterday, my mother attended the 10 PM show of 'Dhabkaaro'. As the crowd was exiting the lift, a heavy ceiling tile suddenly collapsed and fell onto the people below. Two people were injured badly and bleeding, and heavy tile pieces hit my mother's head.
While accidents can happen, the theatre staff's reaction was absolutely disgusting. They were completely uncooperative. Nobody stepped forward to offer basic first aid, medical support, or even a glass of water to the bleeding and injured patrons. We had to literally shout and threaten to call the police just to get them to act, and even then, they helped completely half-heartedly.
We are now dealing with significant medical expenses, and the theatre management hasn't even had the decency to offer a simple apology. They clearly do not care about the safety or lives of their customers. Avoid this theatre at all costs unless you want to put your life at risk.

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Phadnis
featured_reviews.review_text:
Roxy Cinemas, Charni Road is an Art Deco-style single-screen theater located in South Mumbai. While it offers a nostalgic and budget-friendly movie-going experience, recent reviews suggest that the quality of its facilities has significantly declined over time.
Affordable ticket pricing makes it a popular spot for college students and families looking for a low-cost outing.
Many visitors praise the sound quality and screen clarity, noting that it provides a decent viewing experience despite being an older venue.
The seating is frequently criticized for being torn, uncomfortable, or poorly maintained, with some reviewers noting a lack of cleanliness in the auditorium.
Management issues are a common theme in complaints, specifically regarding long exit processes, unhelpful staff, and unsanitary restroom conditions.
The food court offers classic cinema snacks like popcorn and samosas, though some guests find the pricing to be high relative to the theater's overall quality.
Overall, it is a suitable choice
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: We’re glad you enjoyed the nostalgic vibe, sound quality, and value pricing, and we truly appreciate your detailed perspective as we continue working to improve the overall experience.

featured_reviews.name: Stringzzz
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Metro INOX Cinema, and my overall experience was extremely enjoyable and comfortable. This cinema hall perfectly blends a classic feel with modern movie-watching amenities, making it a great choice for both regular viewers and cinema lovers who appreciate a well-maintained theatre.

The screen and sound quality were excellent. The visuals were sharp, bright, and immersive, which made the movie even more engaging. The sound system was well balanced—loud enough to create impact without being overwhelming. Dialogues were clear, and background music and effects were crisp, enhancing the overall cinematic experience.

The seating arrangement deserves special mention. The seats were comfortable, well-spaced, and offered a clear view of the screen from almost every angle. Legroom was sufficient, allowing for a relaxed experience even during a long movie. The auditorium was clean and well maintained, which added to the comfort level.

The ambience of Metro INOX has a pleasant and premium feel. The lobby area was neat, organized, and not overly crowded. The lighting and interiors give a classy vibe, making the wait time before the show quite comfortable. Entry and exit were well managed, avoiding unnecessary rush or confusion.

Food and beverages were also satisfactory. The snacks counter offered the usual cinema favourites like popcorn, cold drinks, and nachos. While prices are on the higher side—as expected in multiplexes—the quality and freshness were good. The staff at the counter were polite and quick in handling orders, even during peak hours.

Another positive aspect was the staff behavior and overall management. The staff members were helpful, courteous, and ensured smooth operations throughout the show. Ticket checking, seating guidance, and cleanliness were handled efficiently. Restrooms were clean and well maintained, which is an important factor for any public place.

Overall, Metro INOX Cinema provides a reliable, comfortable, and enjoyable movie-watching experience. Whether you’re going for a weekend show with friends, a family outing, or a solo movie break, this place delivers on quality, comfort, and ambience. I would definitely recommend Metro INOX Cinema to anyone looking for a pleasant and hassle-free cinema experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Regal Cinema is one of those classic theatres in Mumbai that carries a lot of nostalgia for many people. I recently watched Kerala Files 2 here, and while the theatre wasn’t very crowded (possibly due to the film itself), the experience reminded me why Regal still has its own charm.

I’ve been coming to Regal since childhood. In its earlier decades, it was considered one of the more prestigious cinemas in the city with a strong reputation. Over time, with the rise of modern multiplexes, that status has naturally changed, but the theatre still retains a certain old-school character that many movie lovers appreciate.

The cinema was clean and well maintained, and the balcony seating still provides a very comfortable and enjoyable movie-watching experience.

Food options are limited compared to multiplexes, but there are still decent snacks available.

Overall, while it may not compete with the luxury of newer multiplex chains, Regal Cinema remains a charming and historic place to watch a film in South Mumbai. For those who enjoy a bit of nostalgia along with their movie, it is definitely still worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Pg
featured_reviews.review_text: A very old historical Regal Cinema, located in Colaba, Mumbai, is a historic movie theater known for its charming ambiance and classic architecture. Established in 1933, it has been a significant part of Mumbai's cultural landscape, showcasing a mix of Bollywood and international films. The cinema features comfortable seating and modern screening technology, providing an enjoyable viewing experience. Its central location in Colaba makes it a popular destination for both locals and tourists. Regal Cinema not only offers a glimpse into the city's cinematic history but also serves as a vibrant hub for film enthusiasts in Mumbai.. inside interior not that great, leg space less too

Regal Cinema has that classic old world vibe you don’t find in modern multiplexes anymore. The moment you step inside, it feels like stepping back in time : vintage decor, high ceilings and a heritage aura that makes the movie experience special.

I watched Tere Ishq Mein here and it felt perfect for this theatre. The sound and projection are solid and the seats though old style actually add to the charm. The whole place has a peaceful and nostalgic feel that makes you enjoy the movie even more.

Located right at Colaba, it’s just a short walk from Gateway of India making it a great spot for a movie + evening outing.

If you love classic theatres and want a break from shiny multiplexes, Regal Cinema is absolutely worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Ameer Shaik
featured_reviews.review_text:
Watched Dhurandhar with my friends at Regal Cinemas, Colaba, and it was an experience worth remembering. From the moment we stepped inside this iconic cinema hall, you could feel its timeless charm — Regal isn’t just a theatre, it’s a piece of Mumbai’s film-going legacy. The interiors have that old-world elegance, and the seating and screen were just perfect for enjoying a movie with energy and comfort.

Dhurandhar itself was an absolute blast on the big screen. The story, performances, and background score hit all the right notes, and the audience reaction around us made it even more enjoyable — laughter, cheers, and applause made it feel like we were part of something bigger together.

Watching this film with friends, surrounded by the classic Regal ambiance, added an emotional layer you don’t get in ordinary multiplexes. The sound was crisp, the visuals vibrant, and the overall vibe made the whole evening unforgettable.

Regal Cinemas at Colaba isn’t just a place to watch a movie — it’s a destination that turns each show into a lasting memory. If you’re in Mumbai and want a cinematic experience with character and soul, this is the place to be. Dhurandhar was great, but watching it here made it unforgettable!

featured_reviews.name: Radhikaa Desai
featured_reviews.review_text:
"Step into old Bombay charm at Regal Cinema !"🎥

Watching a movie at Regal Cinema is like stepping into a slice of Mumbai’s heritage. Built in the 1930s, this iconic art-deco theatre still carries the grandeur of old Bombay. The vintage interiors, high ceilings, and classic design instantly transport you back to the golden era of cinema. 🎥📽

One of the best parts is the ticket pricing–at just around ₹100, it’s far cheaper compared to other multiplexes, making it accessible while still offering a memorable experience. The staff are courteous and helpful, and the upgraded sound and screen quality blend nostalgia with modern convenience.

Located right at the Gateway of India circle, Regal is surrounded by the vibrant energy of Colaba. Parking can be a challenge in this busy area, so arriving early or using public transport is more convenient. The only drawback is the washrooms 🚻, which could be better maintained.

Still, Regal Cinema is more than just a theatre–it’s a cultural landmark. For anyone who loves cinema, architecture, or simply wants to relive the charm of old Mumbai at an affordable price, Regal is a treasure worth visiting.🤌✨️

I came across this beautiful Nandi Bull Statue near Plaza Cinema in Dadar East. It’s a striking and culturally symbolic statue that represents strength, patience, and devotion in Indian mythology. The statue is beautifully crafted and placed right in the middle of a bustling area, making it a peaceful yet eye-catching spot.

featured_reviews.name: Nishad Shahasane
featured_reviews.review_text:
Plaza Cinema is one of Mumbai’s oldest and most famous movie halls, located in the heart of Dadar, just a 5-minute walk from Dadar Station and near Shivsena Bhavan.

It’s a single-screen theatre with around 800 seats and a classic, nostalgic charm. The screen is big, the sound is good, and the hall is clean. Facilities include clean washrooms, drinking water, and parking for cars and bikes (no roadside parking).

Snacks are slightly expensive but easily available. The place is usually crowded, which adds to its lively atmosphere. There is a bus stop nearby named "Plaza" from where you can find BEST buses to various locations across Mumbai.

Overall, Plaza Cinema offers a good, old-school movie experience at affordable prices — a must-visit for anyone who loves vintage theatres.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My recent experience at the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand in Dadar left me with mixed feelings. While the overall service of the Shivneri buses remains commendable, the facilities at the bus stand itself are in dire need of improvement, particularly when it comes to providing adequate shelter and comfort for passengers.

On a rainy day, I found myself at the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand, eagerly waiting for my bus. Unfortunately, my anticipation was quickly dampened, both literally and figuratively, as the facility failed to offer proper protection from the elements. The absence of sufficient shelter made it difficult for passengers to find a dry spot to stand or sit, leaving many of us exposed to the rain. It was disheartening to see elderly passengers and families with children struggling to stay dry while waiting for their buses.

The lack of proper infrastructure at the bus stand was evident. The limited seating arrangements were inadequate for the number of passengers present, and those available were often wet due to the rain. There were no covered waiting areas or even basic shelters to shield passengers from the weather. This situation is particularly concerning during the monsoon season when rain is frequent and heavy in Mumbai. A bus stand as busy and important as Dadar's Shivneri should certainly prioritize the comfort and convenience of its passengers by providing better infrastructure.

Despite these shortcomings, there are several positive aspects to note about the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand. The staff at the stand were courteous and helpful, assisting passengers with their queries and providing timely updates about bus arrivals and departures. The ticketing process was efficient, and I appreciated the digital screens displaying real-time information about bus schedules. This helped in reducing the anxiety of waiting, as passengers could see exactly when their buses were expected to arrive.

Additionally, the cleanliness of the bus stand was maintained reasonably well. Despite the rain, the staff made efforts to keep the area free of litter, which is commendable. The security presence was also reassuring, ensuring that passengers felt safe while waiting for their buses.

However, the positive aspects cannot entirely overshadow the critical need for better facilities. For an otherwise excellent service like Shivneri, enhancing the infrastructure at the Dadar bus stand is essential. Investing in covered waiting areas, more seating, and improved drainage systems to prevent waterlogging would greatly enhance the passenger experience, especially during the rainy season.

In conclusion, while the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand in Dadar excels in terms of service efficiency, cleanliness, and staff courtesy, it falls short in providing basic facilities to protect passengers from adverse weather conditions. Addressing these issues will ensure that passengers have a comfortable and pleasant experience, regardless of the weather.

featured_reviews.name: Pathseeker
featured_reviews.review_text: A great movie theatre experience overall. Comfortable seating, well-maintained ambience, and excellent sound quality. The food options are surprisingly good and add to the experience. A perfect place to relax and enjoy a film.

featured_reviews.name: Asmit Karadbhajane
featured_reviews.review_text: Felt less like a theatre and more like a quiet, plush lounge. Super comfortable seats, rich sound, and a calm, classy vibe throughout. Pricey, yes—but it genuinely feels special. Unapologetically Luxe

featured_reviews.name: Joseph Lalrinhlua
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best theaters in India. They have the biggest non-IMAX screens I have ever seen. The auditorium is ginormous. When i first walked I thought I was walking into an IMAX Audi. Other than the near perfect screen size and the cushioned comfy seats, the place is very neat, clean and tidy. There are 3 normal screens and two insignias with smaller screens (but very pricey). A must visit for cinephiles

featured_reviews.name: RAJHANS TEWARI
featured_reviews.review_text: Honestly speaking this is one of the best theatres in mumbai, comfortable seating and great audio and visual experience even in normal screen. Must visit if you live nearby.

featured_reviews.name: dimpi shah
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a pathetic experience with the food court yesterday. They are out there to make money. A) they said this offer is running via this board as well on screen interval ads. At the counter Mr. Ankit said sorry it's actually not available B) ok I said I want a regular size popcorn he says oops we just ran out of tubs so compulsarily u need to buy a big tub no other option. Please explain me how can a place like Jio and PVR not have tech enabled to run Eazy diner as well as no regular popcorn tubs.

featured_reviews.name: yusuf shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: I went to PVR to watch a movie and had a great experience. The audio and visual quality were top notch and the seating was comfortable. The ambience was nice and the theatre was clean. Staff was polite and helpful. Definitely a good place for a quality movie experience.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text: Maison PVR is a genuine experience of uber luxury and spotless beauty. One of the newest and most beautiful Theatre in town. It is divided in Library rooms (normal premium halls) and Living Rooms (smaller luxury theatres). Both of these are on either sides of lobby. You can sense the difference in ambience, but both the sides are extremely well kept and uniquely curated. Inside the halls you can feel the luxury in their recliners and chairs. Sound system, Screen size and interiors of all theatres are different and unique. Highly recommended place to view your latest movies if you want to experience luxury.

featured_reviews.name: Munavvar ali
featured_reviews.review_text: Nakshathra mall is located near to the dadar railway station. Mall outlets are having local brand shops, ther is no brand shops here. It is below average mall in Mumbai. Only highlight is inox cinema apart from nothing is there.  It is not cleaned inside and not maintained well. Usually outside it is fully crowded because there are number of small shops along the road.

featured_reviews.name: A
featured_reviews.review_text:
A dilapidated mall in filthy condition. The PVR there is single screen and don't allow you inside if you're more than 15 minutes early. The experience of this PVR is different from the regular multi screen PVRs. The quality of the picture on screen was good, good surround sound too. They have limited snacks though. The good part is the snacks were available at slightly lower prices than the regular PVRs. Sandwich was hopeless and there are no samosas. There were nachos, a couple of more types of sandwiches and even pizzas. French fries were available too which were served hot and crispy. The popcorn was nice too.
But this mall and this PVR is completely avoidable.

featured_reviews.name: Arun Spartan
featured_reviews.review_text: Had an awesome experience at PVR Cinemas! The ambience was शानदार, seats were super comfortable, and the audio-visual quality was top-notch. Clean environment and smooth booking process made it even better. Perfect place to enjoy movies!

featured_reviews.name: Manan Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Such a bad theatre and movie watching experience overall.

Sound is poor, seats are bad and food is just average. Not worth the price one bit.

The only thing decent is the anesthetic but that doesn't matter for the movie. I would rather watch at home!

featured_reviews.name: Sumanto Ray Two Mouths Full
featured_reviews.review_text: It's a decent enough cinema hall. The crowd is good. The location is central. Cleanliness is at the top. Seats are not very comfortable, but still, it worked for us. Decor inside the theater gives a feeling of the old-world charm. Loos are very clean. The food is expensive and the waiting area is very hot. Picture and sound quality is also great.

featured_reviews.name: Balkrishna Shroff
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the finest single theatre in Mumbai. Always well maintained. Two big lifts helps to reach theatre on 4th floor very quickly. F&B counter has got a lot of options. The staff is very courteous and helpful. The big screen with Dolby sound adds the movie watching experience. The parking facility in such a busy area is extra bonus.
Worth visiting…

featured_reviews.name: Asim Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text:
Overall, the movie experience at PVR Le Reve was disappointing. The only reason to pick is the convenience for people staying in Bandra West.

Specifically, avoid booking the A row (last row) seats as they do not recline at all, which makes them quite uncomfortable for a long movie. On top of that, the air conditioning was poor and felt like it wasn’t fully switched on, making the auditorium stuffy throughout the show.

featured_reviews.name: Pervin Dumasia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely bad experience with the food n beverage.  Ordered for almost 1000/- rupees--for a single person.  Was served stale samosas. Feeling unwell after a few hours due to this. The coffee was so bad and not what I had ordered. The coffee was replaced---but even that was lackluster and very tasteless. Complained to the manager--chandresh-- who was not trained well enough to address the situation.

After charging so exhorbitantly( for just popcorn, coffee n samosas )---it is a shame that such sub standard food is served to patrons. I am a very tolerant person,  and rarely complain--but this was too much of cheating of customers.

Truly upset and disappointed with PVR.  The relevant authorities need to check their kitchen.  Been to many PVR  theaters before,  including this one---and although the food was never great, it was atleast not so blatantly bad.

featured_reviews.name: Javed R Inamdar
featured_reviews.review_text: Very very low quality Projection. Screen size and seating arrangement is not comfortable as curve screen. Sound is Good. If show is housefull then you have to wait for the washroom just like a general public toilet outside the railway station. I don't know how PVR has granted franchise franchise to Such location. Need change 🙏

featured_reviews.name: Muhammed Golwala
featured_reviews.review_text: The PVR theatre was great with amazing decor, and fantastic Dolby Atmos sound system, However few things needs a big improvement as it's a new place. First and foremost the prices on the food is extremely high which does not make any sense for an item like popcorn 🍿 paying more then a meal at another places. Secondly I wish the staff was a bit more kind and smiling as it reflects their interest in their jobs and improves the customer satisfaction for the place, Third but not least the air condition needs to be better as it gets pretty warm in the theatre. Wish the best for them👍
